prompt: What triggers a notification rule in PI Server 2016 R2 and later?

options.text: A PI tag exceeding its CompDev
Event frames matching the rule's criteria
A PI Vision display being opened

explanation: Notification rules are triggered by event frames. A rule can even be created straight from an Event Frame Generation analysis.

prompt: Which delivery channels do PI Server 2016 R2+ notification rules support? Select all that apply.
explanation: Notification rules support only Email and Web Service delivery channels, and custom delivery endpoints are not supported. Pager and custom channels were part of legacy notifications.

prompt: What is the supported way to deliver these alerts?
scenario: A water utility upgraded to PI Server 2018. Its old PI Notifications 2012 set-up sent SMS messages through a custom delivery channel. The team wants the same SMS alerts with notification rules.

options.text: Re-register the custom channel in PSE
Use email to an email-to-SMS gateway, or the web service channel
Ask AVEVA for the custom channel migration path
Use PI Builder to recreate the channel

explanation: Custom delivery channels are not supported after 2016 R2, and AVEVA declined to provide a migration path for them. Use an email-to-SMS gateway or a web service.

prompt: A site upgrades AF Server to 2.8.5 (2016 R2) but does nothing about its PI Notifications 2012 configuration. What happens?

options.text: Legacy notifications stop working; they must be migrated with the PI Notifications Migration Tool
They convert to PI Vision alerts

explanation: An AF Server 2.8.5 (2016 R2) server no longer supports legacy 2012 notifications. The PI Notifications Migration Tool in %pihome%\Notifications converts them; some legacy features cannot be migrated.

prompt: Order the steps to subscribe a contact to a notification rule in PSE, as in the PI World 2020 lab.

items.text: Open View/Edit Subscriptions on the rule
Drag the contact's delivery endpoint (for example E-mail) into Subscriptions
Use Test Send to confirm delivery

explanation: Subscriptions are configured with View/Edit Subscriptions by dragging a contact's endpoint in, then Check In. Test Send sends a test notification to a contact.

prompt: Match each notification term to its meaning.

pairs.right: The transport, such as Email or Web Service
A contact's specific address on a channel
Link between a rule and a contact's endpoint

explanation: These four objects make up delivery: channel (how), endpoint (where), subscription (who gets which rule) and format (what the message says).

prompt: True or false: a notification can fire when an event starts, when it ends, or both.
explanation: True. AVEVA's 2019 session states notifications can fire on start, on end or both.

prompt: PI Notifications Service runs by default as which virtual account? (Type the account name.)
explanation: The service runs as the virtual account NT SERVICE\PINotificationsService. Its log is %programdata%\osisoft\pinotifications\logs\pinotifications-log.txt.

prompt: Can notification rules be managed in bulk with PI Builder?

options.text: No; PI Builder cannot manage notification rules

explanation: Notification rules cannot be managed in PI Builder, and the DataLink notification add-in shows status but cannot edit rules.

prompt: Messages show '[-109] Value at This Time Already Exists' from tags such as <GUID>_Action. What is the recommended direction?

options.text: Migrate from legacy 2012 notifications, which used 7 PI tags each, to notification rules

explanation: Legacy 2012 notifications used 7 PI tags each (including <GUID>_Action and <GUID>_TimeOffset). Modern notification rules do not rely on these tags, so migration removes the source of the errors.

prompt: What does AVEVA recommend for high availability of PI Notifications Service?

options.text: Running two copies with no clustering

explanation: AVEVA's 2022 recommendation is Windows Server Failover Clustering for PI Notifications Service (and PI Analysis Service).
